title: A Crown for the Wolf Revisited
premise: Quentin Coldharbour has spent thirty years hiding in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot enter, believing himself the last swordspeaker after the Purge. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley to drag him out, he discovers the hunt is a smokescreen: the king is possessed by the Vessel, an ancient hunger wearing the crown, and it is devouring every gifted soul in the realm to complete its rebirth. Quentin joins a ragged band of survivors—a disgraced huntress, a child who speaks to stone, and the king's estranged daughter—and learns that unbinding the king requires an oath-sacrifice only a swordspeaker can make. In the end, Quentin speaks his final oath to sever the Vessel from the crown, surviving at the cost of his gift, and chooses to return to the valley not alone but with the family he found.
about_author: I. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oaths and curse-formulae before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people bound by promises they regret, and live somewhere deliberately off the map.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Establishes daily life in the Hollow: Quentin mends fences, hides his ritual scars, and tends the grave of his old mentor. A wounded stranger stumbles in carrying a royal writ—and dies naming Quentin by a title no one should know. Emotional beat: the dread of a hidden life cracking open.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Ford
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Crown witch-hunters cross into the valley, where their own magic fails but steel does not. Quentin kills for the first time in decades to save a village boy, Merren, who unknowingly carries stone-speech magic. Emotional beat: guilt—the price of survival is paid in blood again.

chapters.title: What the Prisoner Knew
chapters.summary: Huntress Sera Vane's POV. Captured hunter Sera defects, revealing the hunt is a harvest: the Vessel on the throne is consuming the gifted. She offers Quentin the king's true name and a route to the capital. Emotional beat: wary trust between enemies; the first seed of found family.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The trio travels through burned villages where the gifted were taken. Quentin teaches Merren crude control of his gift while wrestling with the oath that binds him never to speak magic again. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Daughter of Cinders
chapters.summary: Princess Isolde's POV. The party is caught smuggling into the capital by the king's estranged daughter, who has been hunting proof of her father's possession. She tests Quentin's claim by showing him the king—hollow-eyed, mouthing words in a dead tongue. Emotional beat: shared isolation; two exiles recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Court of Whispers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Infiltrating the palace masque, the group learns the Vessel's ritual completes at the solstice eclipse—nine days away. Sera is nearly unmasked by her former commander and escapes only through Isolde's betrayal of her own guards. Emotional beat: rising tension; loyalty tested under pressure.

chapters.title: The Oath Unspoken
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the crypts, Quentin finds his mentor's final letters: the last swordspeaker's oath requires willing sacrifice of the gift itself—and likely the speaker's life. He hides this from the others. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; love expressed as concealment.

chapters.title: Nine Bells
chapters.summary: Merren's POV. The eve of the eclipse. The Vessel's hunters storm the safehouse; Merren's stone-speech collapses a street to save them, but Sera is gravely wounded and Isolde is taken to the throne room as the ritual's anchor. Emotional beat: terror and courage; the child becomes the protector.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Wolf
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax. Quentin fights through the eclipsed throne room, speaks the unbinding oath as the Vessel offers him his gift back plus everything he ever lost. He refuses, severs the king, and the backlash burns the magic out of him forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice triumphant over temptation.

chapters.title: Home Is a Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, coda. The king, freed but broken, abdicates toward reform; Isolde begins rebuilding. Quentin returns to the Hollow with Merren and a recovering Sera—not to hide, but to build a refuge for the gifted. Emotional beat: resolution; survival's price paid, and worth it.
